Dallas, Texas

Greenland Hills

Also known as the M Streets — a historic Dallas neighborhood celebrated for Tudor Revival homes, mature trees, walkability, and a strong sense of place.

Official Conservation District boundary: the northern edge follows the alley between McCommas Boulevard and Longview Street; Longview itself is not presented as a neighborhood street here.

About the neighborhood

Greenland Hills was developed primarily during the 1920s and 1930s and is best known for one of Dallas's strongest concentrations of Tudor Revival homes. The neighborhood's distinctive architecture, brick streetscapes, mature canopy, and central location have made it one of the city's most recognizable residential districts.

The area is protected by Conservation District No. 9, commonly called the M Streets Conservation District. The district was established to conserve the neighborhood's architectural and cultural character while guiding renovation, additions, and new construction.

Neighborhood streets

  • McCommas Boulevard
  • Monticello Avenue
  • Mercedes Avenue
  • Merrimac Avenue
  • Morningside Avenue
  • Ridgedale Avenue
  • Vanderbilt Avenue
  • Vanderbilt Place

Official boundaries

NorthAlley between McCommas Boulevard and Longview Street
EastGreenville Avenue
SouthAlley between Vanderbilt Avenue and Goodwin Avenue
WestU.S. 75 / North Central Expressway
Typical home-price range $800,000–$1,850,000+

What residents value

  • Historic architecture
  • Mature tree canopy
  • Walkability and neighborhood identity
  • Access to Lower Greenville and central Dallas
  • Conservation-district protections
